findings.claim: The helper retries every Exception, including permanent failures, so non-retryable errors can repeat work and delay failure handling.
evidence: evals/cases/case_06/src/retry.py catches Exception without classifying whether the failure is transient or retryable.
A runtime probe with attempts=3 confirmed that both ValueError and PermissionError operations were invoked three times before the original exception was raised.

findings.claim: Retries occur immediately with no delay, backoff, or jitter, allowing a failing dependency to be hit in a tight loop and amplifying overload during an outage.
evidence: evals/cases/case_06/src/retry.py calls operation() on each loop iteration without any sleep or backoff calculation.
A runtime probe of three consecutive TimeoutError failures completed all three attempts in approximately 0.000007 seconds.

findings.claim: The helper accepts arbitrary operations and can repeat a side effect when an attempt commits work but raises before acknowledging success, causing duplicate production actions.
evidence: evals/cases/case_06/src/retry.py unconditionally invokes the same operation again after any Exception and provides no idempotency key or safeguard.
A runtime probe whose first invocation recorded a committed side effect and then raised TimeoutError returned successfully on retry with the side effect recorded twice.

findings.claim: Non-positive attempts values are not validated and fail with an internal AssertionError before the operation is called, producing an unstable and misleading API failure mode.
evidence: For attempts=0 or attempts=-1, the loop in evals/cases/case_06/src/retry.py never runs and last_error remains None before the assertion.
Runtime probes confirmed that attempts=0 and attempts=-1 each raised AssertionError and invoked the operation zero times.

uncertainties: No production call sites are present in the case, so caller-level exception filtering or idempotency controls cannot be assessed.
